# Supported keyboard layouts

<!-- Generated by tools/generate_docs.py from src/typoshift/layouts/data. Do not edit. -->

Every mapping is extracted from the [xkeyboard-config](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xkeyboard-config/xkeyboard-config) database by `tools/generate_layouts.py` (vendored sources in `tools/xkb`). Only the base and Shift levels are modelled. Dead keys are reproduced: a dead key followed by a letter composes (Greek `;` then `e` gives `έ`), and a dead key followed by a space gives the spacing accent.

## Layouts versus languages

A layout defines which character each physical key produces. A language decides which reconstruction is plausible. TypoShift keeps the two apart:

- Conversion is purely physical. It recovers the keystrokes under the source layout and replays them under the target layout.
- Each candidate is scored against the language models of the target layout's languages (configurable with `layout_languages`).
- Layouts whose base and Shift levels are identical produce identical candidates. For example, Polish (Programmers) is identical to English (US) and needs AltGr for Polish letters. TypoShift reports the first such layout and lists the others as `equivalent_layouts`. The language model, not the layout, decides whether the text is English or Polish.

## Platform differences

The XKB definitions match the standard Windows layouts for letters. Punctuation can differ on other platforms. macOS "Russian" (not "Russian - PC"), macOS "Arabic" and Hebrew-QWERTY are different layouts and are not built in. You can add them as custom layouts (see `docs/CUSTOM_LAYOUTS.md`).

## Key rows

Keys are listed left to right. `·` means the layout has no character on that key at that level. `LSGT` is the extra ISO key next to left Shift, and `BKSL` is the backslash key.
